=====================================================================
INTERVIEW TRANSCRIPT
=====================================================================
Interview Title:    Whistleblower Interview — Environmental Compliance
Interview ID:       WB-2024-0119
Date:              June 14, 2024
Time:              09:00 – 11:30 CST
Location:          Chicago, Illinois, United States
Interviewer:       Margaret "Maggie" O'Sullivan, Esq.
                   (Special Counsel, SEC Whistleblower Office)
Co-Interviewer:    Robert Chen Jr. (Senior Investigator, EPA)
Witness:           John Smith
                   (Former Environmental Health & Safety Manager,
                   Halcyon Petrochemical Corp.)
Note:              Witness testified under pseudonym per
                   whistleblower protection agreement.
=====================================================================

[09:00:15] MARGARET O'SULLIVAN:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Good morning. I'm Maggie O'Sullivan, and this is my colleague
Robert Chen. Please state your name for the record.

[09:00:30] JOHN SMITH:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
My legal name is John Smith, but that's a pseudonym. My real
name is on file with your office. I was the EHS Manager at
Halcyon Petrochemical in Gary, Indiana, from 2019 to 2024.

[09:01:00] ROBERT CHEN JR.:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Mr. Smith, can you describe your role at Halcyon?

[09:01:15] JOHN SMITH:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
I was responsible for environmental compliance across three
facilities: the Gary refinery, the Whiting terminal, and a
storage depot in East Chicago. I reported to the VP of
Operations, Sarah Goldberg, and she reported to the CEO,
William "Bill" Harrington III.

[09:02:00] MARGARET O'SULLIVAN:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Let's go to the events of March 12, 2023. What happened?

[09:02:20] JOHN SMITH:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
There was a chemical release at the Gary refinery. Approximately
14,000 gallons of benzene leaked into a drainage channel that
feeds into the Grand Calumet River. The leak was detected by
a sensor at 02:47 AM, but the alarm system failed. It wasn't
discovered until 6:30 AM when a night-shift operator, Miguel
Hernández, noticed the smell.

[09:03:15] ROBERT CHEN JR.:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Why did the alarm fail?

[09:03:22] JOHN SMITH:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Because it had been disabled. I have documentation showing
that Sarah Goldberg authorized disabling the alarm system
in February 2023 to prevent "nuisance alarms" during a
maintenance overhaul. She sent an email to me and to Tomás
García, the plant manager.

[09:04:00] MARGARET O'SULLIVAN:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Do you have that email?

[09:04:08] JOHN SMITH:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
I do. It's in the packet I gave to your office last month.
The email was sent from s.goldberg@halcyonpetro.com on
February 8, 2023, at 4:15 PM.

[09:04:45] ROBERT CHEN JR.:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Who else knew about the disabled alarm?

[09:04:55] JOHN SMITH:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
At least a dozen people. There was a meeting on February 10th
at the Gary facility. Attendees included Sarah Goldberg,
Tomás García, myself, a safety consultant named Dr. Elizabeth
Fitzgerald, and several shift supervisors. The minutes were
recorded by a junior EHS coordinator, Ahmed Al-Mansouri.

[09:05:50] MARGARET O'SULLIVAN:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
What happened after the March 12 release?

[09:06:00] JOHN SMITH:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
The company downplayed it. The official report to the Indiana
Department of Environmental Management claimed only 800 gallons
were released. Sarah Goldberg told me to revise my incident
report. When I refused, she had HR — a woman named Patricia
O'Brien — issue me a written warning for "insubordination."

[09:06:55] ROBERT CHEN JR.:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Did you report the discrepancy to anyone outside the company?

[09:07:05] JOHN SMITH:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
I contacted the EPA Region 5 office in Chicago on April 3rd.
I spoke with a compliance officer named David Kim. He took my
initial statement but said he needed to escalate it. Two weeks
later, I received a call from someone claiming to be from the
EPA — but I now believe it was a private investigator hired by
Halcyon. The caller ID showed "Kessler & Associates."

[09:08:10] MARGARET O'SULLIVAN:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Kessler & Associates — do you know that firm?

[09:08:18] JOHN SMITH:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
I do now. They're a Chicago-based firm that specializes in
corporate counter-intelligence. Their CEO is a former FBI agent
named Frank Kessler. I believe Halcyon's general counsel,
Meredith Vance, hired them. Ms. Vance works out of the
New York office, at 200 Park Avenue.

[09:09:15] ROBERT CHEN JR.:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
How were you retaliated against?

[09:09:25] JOHN SMITH:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
It started subtly. I was excluded from meetings. My budget was
cut. Then in October 2023, I was placed on administrative leave
for "performance issues." In December, I was terminated. My
termination letter was signed by Sarah Goldberg and cc'd to
Meredith Vance and to the CHRO, a man named Kenneth Adeyemi.

[09:10:20] MARGARET O'SULLIVAN:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Were you offered a severance package?

[09:10:28] JOHN SMITH:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Yes. $250,000 in exchange for signing an NDA. I refused.
My attorney, Rachel Zimmerman at Zimmerman & Patel LLP,
advised me not to sign.

[09:11:00] ROBERT CHEN JR.:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Let's talk about other incidents. Was the March 2023 release
isolated?

[09:11:12] JOHN SMITH:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
No. There were at least three other unreported releases. One
at Whiting in July 2022, one at East Chicago in November 2022,
and another at Gary in January 2023. All were small — under
500 gallons each — but all should have been reported under
the Clean Water Act and EPCRA.

[09:12:00] MARGARET O'SULLIVAN:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Did the company have an environmental management system in
place?

[09:12:10] JOHN SMITH:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
On paper, yes. It was certified to ISO 14001. But the audits
were conducted by a firm called EcoVerify Consulting, and I
believe their lead auditor, Dr. James Okafor, was pressured
to soften his findings. I have notes from a call with him
in September 2022 where he expressed discomfort.

[09:13:00] ROBERT CHEN JR.:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Where is Dr. Okafor now?

[09:13:05] JOHN SMITH:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
He left EcoVerify in early 2023. I believe he relocated to
Toronto. I don't have current contact information.

[09:13:35] MARGARET O'SULLIVAN:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
One final question. Are you aware of any other witnesses
who would corroborate your account?

[09:13:50] JOHN SMITH:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Yes. Miguel Hernández, the night-shift operator. Tomás García,
the plant manager. And a former lab technician named Priya
Deshpande. She was fired in August 2023 after she refused
to alter lab results. She now works at a university in
Ann Arbor, Michigan.

[09:14:35] MARGARET O'SULLIVAN:
---------------------------------------------------------------------
Thank you, Mr. Smith. We'll be in touch. This interview is
concluded. Recording stopped at 11:30 CST.

[09:14:45] END OF TRANSCRIPT
=====================================================================
